description: Ten fixed quiz and flashcard prompts for comparing raw JSON acceptance with LearnLoop validation and repair.

cases.content: Underfitting uses a model that is too simple and has high bias. Overfitting models training-specific noise and often has high variance. Regularization limits unnecessary complexity.
Data leakage occurs when information unavailable at prediction time influences training or evaluation. Preprocessing should be fitted only on training data inside each cross-validation fold.
Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are correct. Recall is the fraction of actual positives that are found. F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
K-fold cross-validation divides training data into k folds, trains on k minus one folds, and validates on the remaining fold. The process rotates the validation fold.
L1 regularization can drive coefficients to zero, while L2 regularization shrinks coefficients smoothly. Both discourage excessive model complexity.
Bias is systematic error from an overly simple model. Variance is sensitivity to fluctuations in the training sample. The bias-variance tradeoff balances both.
Training data fits model parameters. Validation data supports model and hyperparameter selection. Test data should remain untouched until final evaluation.
Precision measures how many predicted positives are correct. Recall measures how many actual positives are found. F1 combines precision and recall.
In k-fold cross-validation, the data is divided into k folds and each fold serves as validation once while the others are used for training.
L1 regularization can produce sparse coefficients. L2 regularization shrinks coefficients without usually making them exactly zero.
